subject: LuminateHealth: intermittent HOL blocking causing 500s and token rejections
messages:
From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@luminatehealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Luminate Health Ops <ops@luminatehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Aug 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production errors — 500s and token rejections impacting inference

Hi Monica,

We're seeing a sudden uptick in 500s and token-rejection errors in our production calls to Redwood starting ~07:45 PT. P99 is spiking to 3.5s and about ~2.3% of requests return 500s or "token rejected". This is affecting our triage queues and causing a partial outage for a small subset of users.

Attached is a short dump of recent request IDs and a screenshot of our SLO dashboard. We've pinned the times to two tenant IDs that look correlated. Can someone from Redwood ops confirm whether this is a customer-side config change or something on your priority-lane side?

We need an ETA — this is customer-impacting.

Thanks,
Emily Chen
Director of Platform Engineering
LuminateHealth

Subject: Fwd: Production errors — 500s and token rejections impacting inference

Team — forwarding LuminateHealth's report. Key facts:
- P99 jump and ~2% 500s started ~07:45 PT.
- Customer attaches request IDs; they see it on two tenant IDs but only a subset of traffic is impacted.
- They report "token rejected" messages alongside 500s (appears from runtime).

I've opened OPS-12948 in Jira and included their attachments. Ben/Jonas, can you triage whether this is HOL/head-of-line queuing or a KV-prefetch eviction pattern? This smells like priority lane interference or an aggressive KV eviction policy causing redispatch.

Customer is asking for ETA. Please reply with an interim mitigation ASAP (rate-limits, pinning, or short-term config). I can coordinate comms.

—Monica
Monica Patel

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Emily Chen <emily.chen@luminatehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Aug 2028 08:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production errors — 500s and token rejections impacting inference

Thanks for the signal and the dump, Monica/Emily. Initial findings from quick logs:
- We see a pattern of repeated small prefixes from the impacted tenant IDs. Prefetch hitrate drops sharply just before the 500s.
- Several workers hit KV cache eviction churn at ~07:46; eviction rate + rebalance operations spike.
- When eviction churn happens, some requests hit an empty prefix and get routed through the cold path — this can cascade into HOL blocking when batch lanes wait for KV refill.

Immediate mitigation I recommend (we can apply in the next 10–15m):
1) Temporarily increase per-tenant cache slots (pin those two tenant IDs) to reduce eviction churn.
2) Reduce batch max size for affected pool to avoid head-of-line due to long cold-fetches.
3) Enable a short-term conservative eviction policy for priority lanes (move from LRU-optimistic to sticky window).

Ben, can you validate whether pinning and eviction-policy flip are safe for the dedicated pool they're on? If we do those three, we should see SLO stabilize; ask Monica to tell the customer we'll push changes and follow up.

-Jonas
Jonas Weber
Staff Engineer, Inference Runtime
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Emily Chen <emily.chen@luminatehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Aug 2028 08:55:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production errors — 500s and token rejections impacting inference

Jonas — looks good. Quick notes from infra:
- The tenant is on a Dedicated pool with mixed workloads; current per-tenant slot is 32. We can raise it to 128 for the two affected tenant IDs for a short window; memory headroom exists on the hosts.
- Eviction policy flip can be done via rolling config (no restart). I'll prepare a canary change to the eviction controller and throttle back the max batch size for the pool.
- I'll also add a temporary bypass: any request that has seen >=2 prefetch misses within the last 5s will be accelerated to the cold-path hot-reroute rather than queueing in the normal batch lane (this reduces HOL holding time).

Will push canary in ~20m and watch 10m windows. Monica — please tell Emily we'll apply changes and provide ETA ~25m.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Production errors — 500s and token rejections impacting inference

Emily — quick update: Redwood ops will push a targeted mitigation (pinning + eviction-policy change + batch-size reduction) in ~25 minutes. They expect to see P99 and error rate recover within the first 10 minutes after canary if the hypothesis (eviction churn -> HOL blocking) is correct.

We will:
- Apply temporary pin to the two tenant IDs
- Flip eviction policy to sticky-window for affected hosts
- Throttle batch max size on the impacted pool

I'll follow up with a postmortem plan and a runbook excerpt we will share. Please keep any request IDs you can — Ben/Jonas asked for any additional traces you can push to OPS-12948.

—Monica

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emily Chen <emily.chen@luminatehealth.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 19 Aug 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors — 500s and token rejections impacting inference

Follow-up note for the leadership and CS sync:
- Mitigation was applied 2028-08-18 09:00 PT (pin + policy flip + batch throttle). Customer reported error rate fell from ~2.3% to 0.12% and p99 dropped from 3.5s to ~0.9s within 7 minutes of the canary.
- Root cause appears to be an earlier config drift on the eviction controller that decreased effective per-tenant slot quotas for mixed-tenant hosts. That drift increased eviction churn during a small burst of sticky prefixes from LuminateHealth.
- Action items:
  * Ops: roll a safe guard to detect sudden per-tenant slot changes and alert (OPS-12961).
  * Product: schedule a permanent sticky-window eviction option for high-SLA tenants + self-serve pinning controls (REQ-771).
  * CS/AM: offer LuminateHealth a 30-day SLA credit and coordinate a technical review.

Monica — I'll draft the exec note (1-page) and a short timeline for the postmortem. Evelyn, please add to the customer renewal/expansion brief so leadership has visibility.

—Marissa
